name: Loire Valley
tagline: Renaissance châteaux and the garden of France
summary: The Loire Valley is France's château country, a gentle river valley of Renaissance palaces, vineyards and gardens. See Chambord's double-helix staircase, Chenonceau spanning the Cher river, Leonardo da Vinci's last home at Clos Lucé in Amboise, and the gardens of Villandry, then taste Vouvray and Chinon wines and cycle the Loire à Vélo route.
seasonNote: May to September; many châteaux hold light shows on summer evenings.
arrival: TGV trains from Paris to Tours or Saint-Pierre-des-Corps take about 1 hour.
gettingAround: A car is easiest; château shuttle buses and bike rental work in summer.
cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; service is included in prices.
foodTip: Rillettes de Tours, goat cheeses like Sainte-Maure, tarte Tatin and Vouvray and Chinon wines.
